clue.text: By the sound of it, Saladin's chivalry was a figment of the imagination!

indicators.note: the clue signals that the phrase it describes is to be heard rather than read, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: Saladin was a Muslim sultan, so his mounted warriors were Arabian knights

explanation.surface: A claim that the famed courtesy of the sultan Saladin never really existed.
explanation.walkthrough: Saladin fought the Crusaders; his knights were Arabian, and that phrase said aloud matches the title of the story collection.
explanation.definitionFit: The tales of the Thousand and One Nights are fantasy, so the title stands for something wholly imagined.

clue.text: Logically works out the causes

definitions.meaning: to reason is to think something through step by step

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means thinks logically; as a plural noun it means grounds or motives.

clue.text: Feel it's important for one so senseless

definitions.text: Feel it's important for one so senseless

parts.words: Feel it's important for one so senseless
parts.note: a person lacking sight relies on touch, for instance reading raised dots, so feeling matters to them

explanation.surface: A remark that an insensitive person ought to learn to feel.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without sight is lacking one sense, and touch becomes vital for reading Braille.

clue.text: Give up careless behaviour

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means forsake; the noun means a complete lack of restraint.

clue.text: French town takes the way of greatest accuracy

indicators.note: the town takes the next piece onto its end, so the two are joined in order

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A French resort is chosen as the most precise route.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its older sense means precise or finely discriminating, so the superlative means most exact.

clue.text: Funny, Reg's in the forest, though normally found on cultivated ground

indicators.note: Reg's is in the forest, read the other way round: the forest goes inside Reg's letters
funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are to be put in an odd order

parts.note: the name Reg with its S, taken as letters
the Forest of Arden, the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A man called Reg turns up oddly among the trees, though his sort usually tend fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' looks like a comment on the surface but signals the rearrangement; 'in' means the forest of As You Like It sits inside the scrambled letters, not Reg inside the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: People who tend plants are usually seen on tilled land, a descriptive definition.

clue.text: At the back, drank out of a large mug

indicators.note: the word At is taken back to front, as if read from the back
out signals the letters of drank are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone at the back of the pub drinks from a big mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the back' turns AT into TA; 'out' scrambles DRANK into NKARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a tall drinking vessel with a handle, usually for beer.

clue.text: Keep on going if you've got it

definitions.text: Keep on going if you've got it

parts.words: Keep on going if you've got it
parts.note: the quality that lets a person continue without tiring

explanation.surface: Advice to persevere if you are able.
explanation.definitionFit: It is staying power, the endurance to continue physical or mental effort.

clue.text: Sir Harold's £150 is — and where he keeps it, perhaps

definitions.meaning: an election candidate's deposit, then £150, is returned if he wins enough votes, so a leading politician's money is not at risk
a bank's strongbox where valuables are stored

explanation.surface: A famous politician's cash is secure, and here is where it is stored.
explanation.walkthrough: UK parliamentary candidates lodged a £150 deposit, lost below an eighth of the vote; Sir Harold (Wilson, a prime minister) was in no danger.
explanation.definitionFit: One reading describes a deposit that is not at risk; the other names a secure bank box.

clue.text: Peer round the top of his head

definitions.text: Peer round the top of his head

parts.words: Peer round the top of his head
parts.note: a nobleman wears a small crown encircling his head; peer is a lord, not a look

explanation.surface: Someone glancing around the crown of a man's head.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the small crown worn by members of the nobility on ceremonial occasions.

clue.text: Petty criminals coming in to land without permission

definitions.meaning: people committing a minor wrong against property

definitions.text: coming in to land without permission
definitions.meaning: entering someone's ground uninvited, rather than an aircraft landing

explanation.definitionFit: Both readings describe people who enter another's property without leave.

clue.text: Sharp increase in the water-rate

parts.note: not a bill going up but the level of a river rising suddenly

explanation.surface: Complaint about a steep rise in a household bill.
explanation.definitionFit: An overflowing of water onto land is a sudden surge, read as a rate of water.

clue.text: Speed off to reprove one made reckless by want of hope

definitions.text: made reckless by want of hope

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the word are scrambled

parts.note: to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

explanation.surface: Telling off a speeder who has lost all hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SPEED into DESPE, followed by RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in despair takes wild risks, so reckless through hopelessness describes them.

clue.text: Make out nurse is involved in rolling dice.

indicators.note: the nurse is mixed in with dice being rolled, so all the letters are tumbled together

parts.note: SRN stands for State Registered Nurse, a former British qualification

explanation.surface: A nurse joins in a game of dice.
explanation.walkthrough: SRN and DICE together are shuffled by 'involved in rolling'.
explanation.definitionFit: To make out something is to perceive or detect it, especially with difficulty.

clue.text: At these, people get cross if we're behind them!

definitions.text: At these, people get cross if we're behind them!

parts.words: At these, people get cross if we're behind them!
parts.note: voters mark an X on the ballot, and the electorate stands behind the polls rather than being angry

explanation.surface: People become annoyed when we lag behind.
explanation.definitionFit: At polls voters put a cross by their chosen candidate.

clue.text: And make fun of what a severe judge might do about it.

definitions.text: what a severe judge might do
definitions.meaning: in slang, to send someone up is to sentence them to prison

explanation.surface: A harsh judge's sentencing compared with mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to satirise, and also, informally, to jail.

clue.text: And put one inside for taking a wallet, for instance

definitions.text: And put one inside for taking a wallet, for instance

parts.words: And put one inside for taking a wallet, for instance
parts.note: as a noun the item that holds a wallet, as a verb to take it; the thief may be put inside a prison

explanation.surface: A thief who steals a wallet gets sent to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A pouch sewn into clothing holds a wallet; as a verb it also means to take dishonestly.

clue.text: Change the basis of our economic system

definitions.text: the basis of our economic system
definitions.meaning: the metal currency on which money rests

explanation.definitionFit: Coins in general are small change and form the monetary currency.

clue.text: Holy woman's relatives?

parts.note: a nun is called by the title for a female sibling, so female siblings are read as nuns

explanation.surface: A question about a nun's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Female siblings are relatives; nuns too are addressed by the same title.

clue.text: Had to get all shook up in Egypt to make it sound!

definitions.text: Had to get all shook up in Egypt to make it sound!

parts.words: Had to get all shook up in Egypt to make it sound!
parts.note: an ancient Egyptian rattle produced noise only when shaken

explanation.surface: Someone in Egypt needing a thorough shake-up to be healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the metal rattle used in ancient Egyptian worship, sounded by shaking.

clue.text: Try to avoid taking this action

definitions.text: Try to avoid taking this action

parts.words: Try to avoid taking this action
parts.note: the action taken when trying to dodge is a dodging one

explanation.surface: Advice to steer clear of a particular step.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging or eluding action is what one takes to avoid something.

clue.text: Court disaster if you fail to do it successfully

definitions.text: Court disaster if you fail to do it successfully

parts.words: Court disaster if you fail to do it successfully
parts.note: a lawyer losing a case in court, not tempting fate

explanation.surface: A warning that failure invites catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel argues a client's case; losing it means a disaster in court.

clue.text: One who is won't work for a woman immodestly dressed, it appears!

definitions.text: a woman immodestly dressed, it appears!
definitions.meaning: without a shift, the old word for a chemise

explanation.definitionFit: It means lazy and idle, and read literally means lacking a shift, a woman's undergarment.

clue.text: Illustration in a book from the kitchen?

definitions.meaning: a dish on which food is served

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a printed picture in a book and a dish for serving food.

clue.text: Put up with the need for high electricity charges

definitions.text: Put up with the need for high electricity charges

parts.words: Put up with the need for high electricity charges
parts.note: erected to carry power lines aloft, rather than tolerating big bills

explanation.surface: Grudgingly accepting expensive power bills.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall steel tower is erected to carry overhead power cables.

clue.text: Point aster out-nothing like another plant

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Picking out an aster as nothing like a different flower.
explanation.walkthrough: E, ASTER and O together are rearranged by 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a kind of hybrid rose scented like tea, so a plant.

clue.text: Revives the festivities at Nuremberg?

definitions.meaning: the mass Nazi party gatherings held at Nuremberg

explanation.definitionFit: It means recovers, and names the great Nazi gatherings held at Nuremberg.

clue.text: We hear it won't try the patience if it's a good one!

definitions.text: We hear it won't try the patience if it's a good one!

parts.words: We hear it won't try the patience if it's a good one!
parts.note: patience sounds like patients, so a doctor's good manner will not try those being treated

explanation.surface: Something good that will not test anyone's patience.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a doctor's manner with patients, which if good puts them at ease.
